October 20, 2026
PRESS RELEASE
Apple announces new American Manufacturing Program partners for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro
From U.S. titanium to advanced camera technology, American suppliers are producing key components in the latest iPhone lineup
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced new and expanded partnerships with American companies that are supplying critical materials and components for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.
Through its American Manufacturing Program (AMP), Apple is partnering with Perryman Company, a Pennsylvania-based titanium producer, to supply titanium for Apple products, including iPhone Duo. Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics, headquartered in Delaware, to produce technology for the new variable aperture in the iPhone 18 Pro camera system — the most advanced Apple has ever made.
Apple works with suppliers in all 50 states and supports more than 450,000 American jobs. Last year, the company deepened that commitment by launching AMP, aimed at bringing even more advanced manufacturing and critical component production to the United States as part of Apple’s $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation.
“We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer. “American ingenuity is vital to all our products, from the titanium crafted for iPhone Duo to breakthrough camera innovations in iPhone 18 Pro. We’re proud to work with Perryman and Qnity Electronics to continue expanding our American Manufacturing Program and support U.S. jobs.”
The grade 5 titanium enclosure on iPhone Duo is exceptionally strong, providing amazing durability to the first foldable iPhone. Apple will commit up to $100 million over the next three years with Perryman, a family-owned business and a global leader in manufacturing specialty titanium products. At its site in Houston, Pennsylvania, Perryman melts, forges, and rolls titanium with a minimum of 80 percent recycled content for iPhone Duo.
Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics to build key camera technology for iPhone 18 Pro in the U.S. Qnity, which joined the American Manufacturing Program in March, will produce advanced films essential to the new variable aperture camera system on iPhone 18 Pro. Variable aperture is at the heart of the new 48MP Fusion Main camera, which enables incredible light and depth control. It’s powered by on-device intelligence that automatically lets in more light for darker settings and helps get sharper detail in brighter ones.
Nearly 100 components in iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro — from wireless chips to the silicon that powers key functions across the devices — are produced by American companies and drawn from suppliers in more than a dozen states. That footprint continues to grow, empowering partners across the country to bring new capabilities online:
As part of Apple’s ambitious goal to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030, all direct suppliers are required to power their Apple manufacturing with renewable energy by the end of this decade. These partnerships, which also include the increased use of recycled materials, reflect that broader environmental commitment.
Apple’s commitment to American manufacturing extends to the workers and businesses building the sector’s future. In August, Apple opened its Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston, Texas — the company’s second U.S. manufacturing learning site. Inside the 20,000-square-foot center, Apple engineers train small- and medium-sized businesses on the same processes used to make Apple products, from advanced manufacturing principles for final assembly to design considerations for printed circuit board assembly. The AMC sits within the same Houston facility that builds Apple’s advanced AI servers and will begin manufacturing Mac mini this year.

Tech Mahindra is an Indian multinational information technology services and consulting company. It was formed in 1986 as a joint venture between Mahindra & Mahindra and BT Group. Part of the Mahindra Group, the company is headquartered in Pune and has its registered office in Mumbai.
History
[edit]
In 1986, Mahindra & Mahindra started a 60:40 joint venture technology services outsourcing firm with British Telecom named Mahindra British Telecom (MBT). In 2000, British Telecom committed business of at least £105 million over three years; as a consideration, British Telecom's stake in MBT increased to 43%. MBT primarily served the telecommunications industry in its early years, with British Telecom as its largest client.
In 2006, MBT was renamed as Tech Mahindra, and it became a publicly-listed company via an initial public offering. In December 2010, British Telecom sold 5.5% of its stake in Tech Mahindra to Mahindra & Mahindra for ₹451 crore. In August 2012, British Telecom sold 14.1% of its stake to institutional investors for about ₹1,395 crore. In December 2012, British Telecom sold its remaining 9.1% stake to institutional investors for ₹1,011.4 crore. This sale marked the exit of British Telecom from Tech Mahindra.
Acquisition and merger of Satyam
[edit]
In the aftermath of the Satyam scandal, Tech Mahindra emerged as the top bidder for a 31% controlling stake in Satyam Computer Services, beating a bid from Larsen & Toubro, in April 2009. After the completion of the acquisition, Satyam Computer Services was renamed Mahindra Satyam in June 2009. Tech Mahindra's stake in Satyam increased to 42% through a preferential share allotment in July 2009.
.jpg)
A building in the Bangalore campus of Tech Mahindra c. 2017
In 2010, Mahindra Satyam and Morpho were awarded a contract by UIDAI to implement the biometric identification system for the Aadhaar programme. Mahindra Satyam, along with Tech Mahindra, was the official IT services provider for the 2010 and 2014 FIFA World Cups.
Tech Mahindra announced its merger with Mahindra Satyam on 21 March 2012, after getting approval of the two company boards. The new organization would be led by Anand Mahindra as Chairman, Vineet Nayyar as Vice Chairman, and C. P. Gurnani as the CEO and Managing Director. On 25 June 2013, Tech Mahindra completed the merger to become India's fifth largest software services company with a turnover of $2.7 billion. The merger diversified Tech Mahindra's revenue mix, with the telecommunication vertical's share declining from over 90% in 2009 to 47% in 2013.
Later years
[edit]
In 2013, Mahindra Group company Mahindra Engineering Services (MES) merged with Tech Mahindra. In 2015, Tech Mahindra and Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) jointly purchased a controlling stake in Pininfarina S.p.A., an Italian automotive and industrial design company. By March 2016, Tech Mahindra's post-tax earnings had surpassed that of M&M. Tech Mahindra was ranked 5th among India's IT firms and overall 47th on the Fortune India 500 list for 2019. Since 2023, Tech Mahindra and FIDE have organized the Global Chess League, an over-the-board rapid chess league. In 2025, Tech Mahindra was one of the eight entities selected by the IndiaAI Mission to develop a sovereign foundation LLM.

Mr. Keshub Mahindra was and will always remain a source of inspiration for the entire Mahindra Group. He was a man of principles and ensured that the organisation remained rooted in ethics, values and good corporate governance. He was known for his astute business acumen that helped in transforming Mahindra into a diversified federation of companies. His compassion, and people-centric approach made him a global business icon, who was much loved and respected.

Would you be open to a 2-line answer on how this applies to large enterprise AP teams?

Alex at Ledgerline
